problem: Global routing is said to assign nets to "regions or tracks", but the exam trap correctly says global assigns regions while detailed routing picks exact tracks. The word "tracks" in the definition contradicts the trap and can confuse a student about where track assignment happens.
fix: Global routing assigns each net to routing regions (or global corridors) and estimates congestion; detailed routing chooses the exact tracks, widths, spacing and vias.

problem: Saying each via "adds resistance and capacitance" overstates the capacitance. A via is mainly a resistance and a reliability risk; its capacitance is small next to the wire it joins.
fix: A via is a metal-to-metal connection between layers; each via adds series resistance and is a possible failure point.

problem: "Every CMOS chip uses this backend flow" is too strong. Hand-drawn analog, RF and small full-custom chips skip standard-cell floorplanning and placement, even though they still end in GDSII and signoff.
fix: Digital CMOS chips built from standard cells use this backend flow; full-custom analog and RF blocks are drawn by hand but still go through DRC, LVS and GDSII.
